sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: An erect perennial herb, usually 30–50 cm tall but sometimes reaching 1.5 m. It grows in dry, well-drained grassland, hedge banks, waysides and woodland margins, in sun or partial shade. Its pinnate leaves have alternating large and small leaflets; yellow, five-petalled flowers form a long spike. Hooked fruits contain one or two seeds and cling to animals or clothing.

sections.title: Uses and distinction
sections.text: Traditional medicinal use is documented, but the sources consulted do not establish food use or toxicity. Agrimonia procera is a related species with overlapping vegetative features; mature fruits are among the more reliable characters used to distinguish them.
